headline: Protein language models predict disorder, binding, localization and mutation effects
label: Protein Language Model Prediction
summary: Recent preprints pair protein language model and transformer representations with structural, physical, and benchmarking constraints for mutational and…
synthesis: The dominant thread is transformer or protein language model representations applied to prediction tasks beyond single-site stability: disordered-protein ensemble generation (IDPForge), multi-compartment subcellular localization (DualLoc), IDP-binding site prediction from ESM-2 embeddings (IDBSpred, ROC AUC 0.87), and sequence-only prediction of mutation-induced interaction changes (eSIG-Net). Not every entry shares this basis. DeepISO combines graph convolution with random forest and logistic regression for isoform-specific interaction rewiring, and the physics-informed CNN/GCN model integrates biophysical mutational energetics to improve extrapolation. What is new is the combination of language-model or structural encodings with explicit physical or structural constraints. The TCR-pMHC and drug-target entries extend similar transformer-based designs to immune recognition and affinity prediction.
